core: for statement iteration over an iterable
outOfScope: break, continue, and loop else clauses

claims.claim: A Python for statement iterates over the items of an iterable and executes its suite once for each item, assigning each item to the loop target.
range() generates an arithmetic progression; its stop endpoint is not included.
The range object supplies successive values when iterated rather than constructing a list of all values.
enumerate(iterable, start=0) returns an enumerate object whose iterator yields count-and-value tuples; its count begins at start.
Multiple loop targets can unpack each pair yielded by enumerate into a position and a value.
